chunks: Salih ibn Uqba from Abdullah ibn Muhammad and Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever feeds a wealthy believer, it is for him (as recompense) equal to freeing one neck from the children of Ismail, rescuing him from slaughter; and whoever feeds a needy believer, it is for him equal to freeing one hundred necks from the children of Ismail, rescuing them from slaughter.

key_terms.رَقَبَةً: Neck (metaphor for a slave/person to be freed)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for feeding a wealthy believer versus a needy believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to illustrate the hierarchy of charity, where the spiritual weight of feeding a needy believer vastly outweighs that of an affluent one, akin to the immense merit of freeing a hundred slaves. This comparison to the progeny of Ismail (AS) evokes the historical context of the sacrifice, framing sustenance as a means of deliverance from spiritual and physical distress. It underscores the Shia emphasis on prioritizing the poor in acts of benevolence to maximize divine reward.

en.hubeali: Salih Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad and Yazeed Bin Abdul Malik,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who feeds an affluent Momin would have for him (Recompense) equating (freeing of) a neck from the children of Ismailas and retrieving him from the slaughter; and the one who feeds a needy Momin, would have for him (Recompense) equating to (freeing) one hundred necks from the children of Ismailas, retrieving them from the slaughter’.
en.sarwar: 19. Salih ibn ‘Aqabah has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad and Yazid ibn ‘Abd al-Malik from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whoever feeds an affluent believer it is equal to setting free a slave from the descendents of Isma’il and rescuing him from slaughter. Whoever feeds a needy believer, it is equal in reward for him to set free one hundred slaves from the descendents of Isma’il and rescue them from being slaughtered.”
